identityCollisions.detail: more than one declaration reduces to this identity; the surface's id is a slug and carries no line, so these declarations are not separately addressable through it. Check the sites before calling it a source-side duplication: discovery is a static scan and is blind to `when` selection, so declarations in mutually exclusive branches collide here while at most one of them exists in any given build. That is a limitation of the identity (it has no configuration dimension), not necessarily a defect in the source

title: Reprobuild case addressability through the canonical `ct test` surface

unaddressableSources.detail: imports the vendored ct_test_unittest_parallel shim instead of std/unittest. Note what does NOT happen: the provider's `frameworkForImport` matches the literal names `unittest`, `unittest2` and `unittest_parallel`, and `ct_test_unittest_parallel` is none of them — so no framework is detected, no `detected but not implemented` warning is emitted (the workspace response carries zero of those), and the file falls through the same generic path as any non-test source, reported as `no Nim unittest imports detected in file`. Implementing unittest_parallel support upstream would therefore NOT recover these rows; not importing the shim does, which is what 38 sources did. The companion .md says why the one that is left keeps the import
declares no literal suite/test of its own; any cases it contributes are declared in the modules it imports, which are discovered separately under their own identities
